exercises.name: Pullover (Dumbbell)

source_english.description: Pullover (Dumbbell) moves the resistance from overhead toward the chest using a controlled shoulder-extension path.
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your head at one end and your feet on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell with both hands and extend your arms straight above your chest.
Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, slowly lower the dumbbell behind your head until you feel a stretch in your chest and shoulders.
Pause for a moment, then raise the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep the trunk braced.
Keep the elbows softly bent while the resistance travels from overhead toward the chest.
Finish each repetition under control.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable range and stop if control or alignment deteriorates.

exercises.name: Push Press

source_english.description: A barbell push press uses a shallow leg drive to propel the bar from the shoulders to overhead lockout.
instructions: Hold the barbell at the upper chest with feet about shoulder-width apart.
Brace the trunk and dip slightly by bending the knees while keeping the torso upright.
Drive through the feet and press the bar overhead as the legs extend.
Lower the bar to the shoulders under control and reset.
form_cues: Keep the dip vertical.
Finish with the bar over the mid-foot.
Use the legs to start, not to squat deeply.
common_mistakes: Turning the dip into a front squat.
source_english.safety_note: Use a rack and clear overhead space before pressing.

exercises.name: Renegade Row (Dumbbell)

source_english.description: A renegade row combines a high plank with alternating dumbbell rows while the hips resist rotation.
instructions: Place two dumbbells on the floor and set up in a high plank with hands on the handles and feet wide.
Brace the trunk and row one dumbbell toward the ribs without twisting the hips.
Lower it to the floor, then row the opposite dumbbell.
Continue alternating while keeping the plank line stable.
form_cues: Widen the feet for balance.
Pull the elbow toward the ribs.
Keep the shoulders and hips square.
common_mistakes: Using a weight too heavy to set down quietly.
source_english.safety_note: Use stable dumbbells and stop if the wrists or lower back cannot remain aligned.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge (Barbell)

source_english.description: The barbell reverse lunge steps one foot backward, lowers both knees, then pushes through the front foot to stand.
instructions: Start by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart and a barbell resting on your upper back.
Take a step backward with your right foot, landing on the ball of your foot.
Bend both knees to lower your body until your left thigh is parallel to the ground.
Push through your left heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat with the other leg.
form_cues: Keep the feet planted.
Track the knees with the toes.
Keep the chest and trunk controlled.
source_english.safety_note: Use a depth and load that allow a stable knee and hip path.

exercises.name: Seal Row (Barbell)

source_english.description: Lie face down on a flat elevated bench and row the barbell from below the chest toward the ribs.
instructions: Lie face down on a flat elevated bench with a barbell hanging below your chest.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width with palms down.
Pull the bar toward the underside of the bench while keeping your chest and hips on the pad.
Lower the bar until both elbows are straight and the plates are still.
form_cues: Keep the chest supported or torso upright.
Drive the elbows toward the ribs.
Lower until the arms lengthen.
common_mistakes: Lifting the chest from the pad.
Shrugging instead of pulling the elbows.
Letting the weight fall on return.
source_english.safety_note: Keep the torso supported or upright so the shoulder is not jerked by the cable or bar.

style.framing: Full figure and all required equipment/supports visible within a square. Scale and use a three-quarter view to expose the specified contacts without changing anatomy, equipment, grip or technique.
style.no_invention: Technique, equipment and muscles come only from the attached exact catalogue record. No extra attachments, numerical weights, brands or exact angles absent from the source.

scene.single_phase: Palms-down wrist-extension endpoint with thighs supporting forearms
scene.composition: Sit on a bench, feet flat. Both forearms REST on thighs and wrists extend beyond the thigh edges. Both hands hold a single barbell overhand, palms DOWN; lift backs of hands in wrist extension while forearms/elbows remain supported and still. Honor the source trunk-against-support cue with bench back support, without inventing an angle. Show hand orientation, thigh support and whole bar; no palms-up wrist curl, elbow-driven biceps curl or forced elbow lockout.

source_instruction_quotes.text: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and hold a barbell with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Rest your forearms on your thighs, allowing your wrists to hang off the edge.
Slowly curl your wrists upward, bringing the barbell towards your body.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back down to the starting position.

prompt_payload.reference_role: Human appearance/proportions/materials only. Never copy pose, equipment or muscle targets from a reference.
